# Pin which events the calendar's getDayRecords returns for a day

## Welcome 👋

Neo ships a full calendar component, and its events live in a data store. `Neo.calendar.store.Events#getDayRecords(date)` answers "which events belong to this day?". Its rule is simple, and a bit surprising: an event counts only when it **starts and ends** on that day. Pin the rule with a spec. No test covers the calendar's data layer yet.

This is a **good first issue** for Hacktoberfest 2026. It needs Node.js and a clone of this repository: no Docker, no AI setup.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reserved for first-time Neo.mjs contributors.** The maintainer team will not claim, edit, or implement this issue through **2026-10-31**. Comment here to claim it, and ask anything on this issue.

**Set up once:** follow [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone), including `npm run bundle-browser-deps`: without it the unit suite selects zero tests.

## Where things live

- Source: `src/calendar/store/Events.mjs` (`getDayRecords(date)`, sorted by `startDate` ascending), with its model `src/calendar/model/Event.mjs`
- New test file: `test/playwright/unit/calendar/EventsStore.spec.mjs` (the folder is new)
- Pattern to copy: `test/playwright/unit/data/Store.spec.mjs` (creating a store with `data`)
- Tip: `Neo.create(EventsStore, {data: [{id, title, startDate, endDate}, …]})` with `Date` objects works directly.

## What to cover

| Events in the store | `getDayRecords(<that day>)` returns |
|---|---|
| one that starts and ends on the day | that event |
| two same-day events added late-first | both, sorted by `startDate`: the store's sorter orders them |
| one that starts on the day and ends after midnight | not returned, on **either** day |
| one on another day | not returned |
| a day with no events | `[]` |

If you think events that span midnight *should* appear on their days (a month view probably expects that), say so on this issue: that is a behaviour change for its own PR.

## Done when

- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/calendar/EventsStore.spec.mjs` exists, following the pattern file's setup.
- [ ] One `test(...)` per table row.
- [ ] Test-only, as above.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/calendar/EventsStore.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` passes.

## Out of scope

The calendar views, drag-and-drop, and time zones.

## While you wait for review

You just pinned one small piece of a multi-threaded application engine: in Neo.mjs your app's code runs inside a web worker, and the main thread only paints. Two things worth ten minutes:

- **See the part nobody expects.** Run `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` and `npm run server-start`, open `apps/workstation/`, and drag a tab out of the browser window. It becomes its own OS window, still running, with the same component instances and the same worker. [Benefits: Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains why that is possible.
- **Your coding agent can go much further here.** The skills this repository's AI maintainers work with are published on npm as [`neo-agent-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/neo-agent-skills), and they need no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core. With Claude or GPT beside you, the `help wanted` issues are within reach after this one.
